messages:
Anya: Quick question — we have a customer asking that all inference for their EU tenants use the EU region and an EU-quantized model variant (p6q-eu). Can we define a clean routing contract for this that handles missing variants and fallbacks?
Tom: Do they need guaranteed local-only execution or is soft-residency ok?
Anya: Hard requirement: no token leaves EU data plane. So local-only for inference. Metadata can be recorded in control plane outside EU if anonymized.
Chris: That means active/active with model parity across regions is required for them. If p6q-eu isn’t available on a specific pool, we need a deterministic rejection or a consent flow, not blind fallback to p6-us.
Maria: Agreed. Also the quantized variant may produce slight output diffs. We should surface a compatibility flag in the response header so app can decide to accept or re-run with a verified variant.
Tom: Proposal: routing policy priority list: 1) exact tenant + region + model variant, 2) exact tenant + region + compatible variant (same model family + compat bit), 3) reject with structured error and a link to self-serve migration instructions. No cross-region fallback.
Chris: How do we define "compatible variant"? e.g., different quant levels or fp16 vs int8?
Anya: We define a compatibility matrix per model in the catalog. Matrix rows: variant id, family, deterministic-semantics-score threshold, tokenization-compatibility boolean. Stored in model-catalog service and versioned.
Maria: Implementation detail: proxy should validate header X-Model-Variant and consult catalog cache. If not in cache, proxy returns 412 with message: "variant-unknown; control-plane-syncing". 
Tom: For cold regions where variant binary isn't present, we can trigger async artifact promotion (prefetch) but still respond with 202-based acceptance pattern or queue? That might violate local-only constraint.
Chris: Exactly — prefetch is allowed but must stay within EU. If artifact promotion requires transferring from another region, disallowed. Prefetch only if artifact already mirrored to EU storage.
Anya: TL;DR: obey strict region-only rule, never fallback cross-region. If variant missing, return structured error. Offer an operator path to mirror artifacts to region.
Maria: Telemetry: emit a metric for "variant-missing-per-tenant" and increment a counter with labels (tenant, model_family, region). Also add a sample payload with diff-score when compatible fallback is used for other customers.
Tom: What about canary/rollouts where p6q-eu is slightly different but we want to test? We can allow an opt-in header X-Canary-Model=true that only works for tenants in a special whitelist and still enforces region boundary.
Chris: Ops note — deploy-bot: ensure model-catalog publishes digest and signed manifest to regional artifact stores during model onboarding.
Anya: Action items: @Tom to draft routing policy text (PR to routing-service) by EOD Wed; @Chris to add catalog compatibility matrix schema; @Maria to add metrics + header contract for responses.
deploy-bot: noted — created ticket INF-2389 for artifact mirroring checklist.
Maria: Also recommend adding a short CLI command for customers to request EU mirroring with an estimated time ETA if artifact not present. Saves support chats.
Tom: Sounds good. If no objections, I'll open the PR tomorrow.
Chris: No objections from me. :+1:
Anya: Thanks everyone — keeping this strict makes auditing + legal reviews easier. We'll sync again if the catalog design changes.
